rationale: A wins because it turns the no-pilot claim into its own beat-specific story: "Skydio says its power-line drones fly with no pilot at all — regulators will want specifics." B notices the same issue, but leaves it as a proof bullet under "Skydio's pilotless inspection drone wants to take the lineworker off the truck," a headline that also invents a lineworker/truck replacement frame the update never supplies. Both sets have usable bones, but A gives the founder cleaner, more defensible pitch lanes.
gaps_in_A: "Power-line and substation inspection is dangerous, manual, and expensive work utilities have wanted to automate for years" imports market context that is not in the update; source it or downgrade it to a proof need.
"live, contracted enterprise product" overstates the facts; the update says contracts with several US utilities, not live deployments or contract scale.
"first major public proof point since the consumer exit" is a chronology claim the update does not prove. If Skydio had other enterprise proof points, this falls apart.
"wildfire-risk mitigation" is a plausible adjacent beat, but the release facts never mention wildfire risk; do not make that the reporter hook without evidence.
gaps_in_B: "take the lineworker off the truck" and "shift from a crewed inspection truck" are not in the update and smuggle in a labor-replacement story without proof.
"Skydio's drone creates safer jobs for lineworkers" is correctly refused, but the first angle still leans on the same unsupported lineworker premise.
The FAA/BVLOS issue is buried in proof/questions instead of becoming a standalone angle; for a no-pilot drone over critical infrastructure, that is a real beat, not housekeeping.
"newsjack-detector" as the next step chases a policy peg before fixing the core launch hole: no named utility customer, no authorization detail, no measured inspection outcome.
